claim: IAM Identity Center comes with multi-factor authentication (MFA) turned on by default, so all Identity Center directory users must sign in with MFA in addition to their user name and password.
question: Is MFA turned on by default for IAM Identity Center directory users?

qualifiers.scope: per IAM Identity Center instance (Identity Center directory users)
qualifiers.condition: Identity Center directory as identity source; not external IdPs

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center comes preconfigured with multi-factor authentication (MFA) turned on by default so that all users must sign in with MFA in addition to their user name and password.

note: d017 current truth. The date of the default change (What's New 2023-11-16) could not be saved: robots.txt refused the page; no history row.

claim: Each Identity Center directory user can register up to 2 virtual authenticator apps and 6 FIDO authenticators, for a total of 8 MFA devices.
question: How many MFA devices can one IAM Identity Center user register?

evidence.quote: Each user can register up to two virtual authenticator apps, which are one-time password authenticator applications installed on your mobile device or tablet, and six FIDO authenticators, which include built-in authenticators and security keys, for a total of **eight** MFA devices.

claim: IAM Identity Center does not create customer managed policies or permissions boundaries in member accounts: you must create them in advance in each account where you assign the permission set, with a matching name and path, or the assignment fails.
question: What must exist in each member account before you assign a permission set that uses a customer managed policy?

values.display: create those policies in advance in each account
values.spoken: create the policy first in every account

values.display: fails to assign the permission set

qualifiers.condition: permission set with customer managed policies or a permissions boundary

evidence.quote: When you add customer managed policies and permissions to a permission set, IAM Identity Center doesn't create a policy in any AWS accounts. You must instead create those policies in advance in each account where you want to assign your permission set, and match them to the name and path specifications of your permission set.
IAM Identity Center fails to assign the permission set if the policy doesn't exist in your member account.

note: d018 (rule). Exam angle: use CloudFormation StackSets to create the policy in every account.

claim: IAM Identity Center configurable AD sync lets you explicitly choose which Active Directory users and groups are synchronized into IAM Identity Center and control the synchronization, for example by pausing and resuming it.
question: What does IAM Identity Center configurable AD sync do?

values.display: explicitly configure the identities in Microsoft Active Directory
values.spoken: you choose which AD users and groups sync

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center configurable Active Directory (AD) sync enables you to explicitly configure the identities in Microsoft Active Directory that are automatically synchronized into IAM Identity Center and control the synchronization process.

note: d016 current truth (replaces AD Sync since 2025-04-17).

claim: In an organization, member accounts can create account instances when the organization instance administrator permits it; for organization instances created after November 15, 2023 the administrator permits creation, while older instances need it enabled manually.
question: When can AWS Organizations member accounts create an IAM Identity Center account instance?

evidence.quote: There is an organization instance of IAM Identity Center in your organization and the instance administrator permits creation of account instances of IAM Identity Center (for organization instances created after November 15, 2023).

There is an organization instance of IAM Identity Center in your organization and the instance administrator manually enabled creation of account instances by member accounts in the organization (for organization instances created before November 15, 2023).

note: d012: account instances arrived in November 2023 (What's New 2023-11-17, robots.txt refused); this page gives the 2023-11-15 boundary only.

claim: You are limited to one account instance of IAM Identity Center per AWS account, and it manages access only for supported applications in the same account and Region.
question: How many IAM Identity Center account instances can an AWS account have?

values.display: one account instance per AWS account

evidence.quote: Account instances are bound to a single AWS account and are used only to manage user and group access for supported applications in the same account and AWS Region. You are limited to one account instance per AWS account.
